description: Universal training principles that apply across all program paths.

principles.name: Progressive Overload
principles.definition: Gradually increase training stress over time (load, reps, hold time, or difficulty).
principles.application: Arnold tracks overload through weight progression (weighted paths) and progression tree advancement (skill paths).

principles.name: SRA Curve
principles.definition: After training stimulus, performance temporarily decreases (recovery), then increases above baseline (supercompensation). Training must happen at the right point in the SRA curve.
principles.application: This is why rest periods, deload weeks, and 48-72h gaps between similar sessions exist.

principles.name: Specificity
principles.definition: Training adaptations are specific to the demands imposed. Heavy singles build max strength. High reps build endurance. Skill holds build neural patterns.
principles.application: This is why phases are structured: accumulation (volume) → strength (intensity) → peaking (specificity).

principles.name: Variation Within Structure
principles.definition: Variation in exercises prevents accommodation, but the core movement pattern stays constant.
principles.application: Back-off variation changes weekly: tempo, paused, deadstop. Same pattern, different stimulus.

principles.name: Fatigue Management
principles.definition: Training accumulates fatigue. Deload weeks allow fatigue to dissipate while fitness is maintained.
principles.application: Deload weeks are non-negotiable. The max(-2) finisher tracks fatigue: if reps trend down, fatigue is accumulating.

principles.name: Motor Learning
principles.definition: Neural adaptations require high-quality, low-fatigue practice. Training to failure creates maladaptive motor patterns (Branscheidt et al. 2019).
principles.application: Skill work is NEVER to failure. Working sets at 60-70% of max hold.

principles.name: Connective Tissue Adaptation
principles.definition: Tendons and ligaments adapt roughly 50% slower than muscles. Rushing progression causes injuries.
principles.application: Beginners don't add weight until 10 pull-ups / 12 dips. First weight additions are small (+2.5kg pull-ups, +5kg dips).
